lots.what_it_is: London sterling silver coffee pot, date letter f for 1901, tapered George II revival form with ebonised scroll handle, 546.9g total (Gowans says Wolfsky & Co Ltd)

asking.venue: AC Silver (UK dealer), William Hutton & Sons Ltd Edwardian sterling coffee pot, SKU W9843
asking.note: ASKING. Page opened 2026-09-30: price GBP 3,450, 568g (18.3 troy oz), 26.1cm high. Same_item: category guide only. Different maker and form, dealer-restored condition, top-end UK retail ask, not a price paid. AUD at an assumed 2.05 per GBP (not looked up live). A retail ceiling only; a pitted pot with a discoloured base at a regional sale will sit far below it.

lots.guide_summary: No same-item or close entry survives. The only entry is one UK dealer asking price for a different Edwardian sterling coffee pot of similar weight (GBP 3,450, about AUD 7,070 at an assumed 2.05). It is a category guide only, so I have left it out of the guide range. There is no sold or unsold evidence. The lot already has a $500 bid (1 bid, checked 30/09/2026).
lots.working: Maximum bids need SOLD evidence and there is none, so keep = 0 and flip = 0. For the buyer, the floor to think about is scrap: about 500g of sterling (total weight less the wooden handle, which is an estimate) x 0.925 = about 462g fine, or about 14.9 troy oz. Times the live silver spot price in AUD per troy oz, less the refiner's margin, gives the melt floor. I could not look up spot today (search budget used up), so no figure is given. All-in = hammer x 1.198, so the current $500 bid is already $599 all-in.
lots.confidence_reason: The hallmarks are clearly read (lion passant, leopard's head, London date letter f, so 1901-02). The maker's punch is worn: on the body it is a lobed or trefoil shape and on the lid a cruciform punch with '& Co Ld' just visible, so I could not confirm Wolfsky. The base colour is unexplained and the only price evidence is one asking price for a different pot.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3, enlarged: lobed maker's punch (worn, not readable), lion passant, leopard's head (crowned leopard not used after 1821, fits the period), lombardic f in a shield, consistent with London 1901-02. Photo 8, the lid bezel: cruciform maker's punch with letters including '&', 'Co' and 'Ld', plus lion passant and leopard's head, so the lid is marked as well. Photos 6 and 7, the base: copper-orange disc stamped '730 31', '1 1/2 Pt', '2' (pattern number and capacity, typical of a retailer or large maker's catalogue). The rim of the foot is silver-coloured but the disc is copper coloured. Photos 1, 2 and 4 show heavy black pitting and spotting on the body, worst low down on the front. Interior (photo 9) is clean. No dents seen, hinge and lid look intact.
lots.condition: Body heavily pitted and spotted, would need professional polishing and some pits may stay. Base disc is copper-coloured: firestain or copper bloom from harsh stripping is possible, but a copper or plated base insert cannot be ruled out from photos. Handle, spout and lid look sound.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the base disc hallmarked, or only stamped '730 31 1 1/2 Pt'? Does the copper colour on the base rub off or test as silver (acid or XRF), or is it copper? Is the 546.9g weight with the wooden handle, and can you weigh it without it? Are there any holes or splits in the pitted areas, and does the lid hinge close firmly?
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. The AC Silver entry was opened and matches what the researcher said (GBP 3,450, William Hutton & Sons, SKU W9843, 568g). Kept as ASKING, category guide only, and left out of the guide range because it is not the same item. The researcher's Kidson-Trigg and Carters leads were snippet-only with no usable price and were not entered, which is correct.

lots.what_it_is: 19th century Tasmanian birdseye huon pine demi-lune dressing table with oval swing mirror, two small drawers and lower shelf, with damage (147 x 104 x 51cm)
lots.guide_summary: No evidence found. No sold, unsold or asking entries survive because none were gathered: the web search budget for the session is used up. I also tried the Gowans and Colville site searches directly and got no past results for this form.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep = 0 and flip = 0. It is also bulky furniture, so a flip would carry large selling and freight costs. All-in = hammer x 1.198.
lots.confidence_reason: The identification is credible from the photos (birdseye figure on the apron, huon pine colour), but there are no marks, some parts may be later, and there is no price evidence.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 5: good birdseye figure on the apron, with a long horizontal split across the apron front. Photo 6: one square back leg has a pale inserted repair block near its base. Photos 7 and 8: good acanthus and flower-head carving on the cabriole centre leg with a scroll foot, and a ragged timber loss along the front edge of the lower shelf. Photos 3 and 4: open joint cracks in the oval mirror frame, mirror glass clear. Photo 9: dovetailed drawer with a darker stained front. The back legs and top are plain and fairly fresh looking, and could be later.
lots.condition: Split apron, repaired back leg, chipped and broken lower shelf edge, cracked mirror frame joints. Carving and birdseye figure are good. Needs restoration.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are the back legs and the lower shelf original, or later replacements? Is the apron split stable, and is the mirror frame loose at its joints? Is the mirror glass original?

lots.what_it_is: Kitchen dresser described as huon pine, restored with replaced back boards, three-shelf plate rack, one drawer, single mesh-panel door (184 x 131 x 45cm)
lots.guide_summary: No evidence found. No sold, unsold or asking entries survive because none were gathered: the web search budget for the session is used up, and a direct Gowans site search returned no past result for this form.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep = 0 and flip = 0. It is large furniture, which means heavy selling and freight costs for any resale. All-in = hammer x 1.198.
lots.confidence_reason: No price evidence, and from the photos I am not sure of the timber (see findings).
lots.key_photo_findings: Photos 1 to 4: honey-coloured dresser with a shaped crest to the plate rack, three shelves with plate rails, one drawer with a turned knob, a single door with two mesh panels, and arched applied panels either side. Photos 4, 12 and 13: the rack back and side boards show wide, bold grain and several large dark knots, which looks more like a European or radiata-type pine than the tight, fine-grained huon pine usually seen. Some panels could still be huon, but I cannot confirm the timber from photos. Photos 8 and 9: dovetailed drawer, and the interior shelves and boards look fresh. Modern gloss finish all over, which matches the restoration.
lots.condition: Restored and repolished, back boards replaced, some knots and marks. Looks sound and usable.
lots.question_for_gowans: How was the timber identified as huon pine? Is it huon throughout, or only in some parts (top, doors, drawer front), with other timbers in the rack and back? Roughly what age is the carcass, and what was replaced besides the back boards?
